summary: Follow-up to the Dec 28th production incident. Reviewed root cause (autoscaler misconfiguration + bursty traffic exposing KV cache eviction behavior), mitigations applied, short-term vs long-term reliability improvements, and plan for testing and runbook updates. Customer requested clearer fallbacks, more observability, and a coordinated load test. Agreed owners and timelines for runbook edits and the test window.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Sable CTO), Liam O'Connor (Sable Head of MLOps), Samira Khan (Sable Platform)

Summary (auto): Postmortem follow up, confirm mitigations, runbook updates, next steps for load test and monitoring.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We'll do a quick recap of the incident from Dec 28, what we did, what we learned, and then agreed next steps. David's gonna lead the technical bits.
[00:14] David Park: yeah hi, hi all. I'll go through a timeline first, I have the Grafana links that Maya will share after the call. This is a high-level timeline, apologies if timestamps are a bit off, this is from our internal logs.
[00:28] Priya Nair: sounds good, thanks. We're mainly here because the outage impacted our inference pipeline for ~2 hours and caused a backlog in batch jobs. We need clear mitigations so this doesn't recur.
[00:43] David Park: absolutely. Root cause we identified: a misconfiguration in the autoscaler policy for Dedicated pools \u2014 the scale-up thresholds were too conservative and combined with a burst of traffic from your batch job pattern it caused a sustained queue. That queue then triggered fallback to smaller model variants in some routes which degraded quality. At the same time we observed KV cache eviction behavior under memory pressure that exacerbated latencies. So two interacting issues.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Can you spell out "KV cache eviction behavior" \u2014 was that an application-level cache or Redwood runtime KV cache?
[01:11] David Park: good question. It's Redwood runtime KV cache \u2014 per-request prefix/KV cache for streaming contexts. Under memory pressure the runtime's cache entries were being evicted aggressively; that increased repeated token computation and messes with effective latency. There was also some jitter introduced by GC on control plane processes, which made autoscaler decisions lag.
[01:29] Samira Khan: interesting, we thought it was a network issue because we saw some 524s. Did you see any network egress limits or VPC problems?
[01:36] David Park: we looked at VPC and network paths \u2014 nothing abnormal there. The 524s were a symptom of the queueing and timeouts at the service edge, not a fabric-level networking outage.
[01:45] Priya Nair: ok got it. So the mitigations you applied during the incident \u2014 what were they and what's permanent?
[01:52] Maya Chen: quick list: we increased autoscaler aggressiveness for your Dedicated pool as an immediate mitigation, added a temporary larger memory headroom config for the KV cache, and rolled back aggressive model fallbacks so requests didn't silently swap to smaller variants. After the incident we pushed two config changes to your environment and scheduled a control-plane patch to reduce GC pause durations.
[02:11] Liam O'Connor: When you say "rolled back model fallbacks" \u2014 isn't fallback part of the graceful degradation we want?
[02:17] David Park: yes, fallback is important but in this case the routing policy triggered fallbacks too early because it was looking at queue length only. We adjusted the policy to consider end-to-end latency percentiles and token progress before falling back. So it's more conservative now.
[02:34] Priya Nair: that helps. We need to ensure quality isn't silently harmed during peak loads.
[02:40] Maya Chen: agreed \u2014 part of the plan is to add a quality signal to the routing decision and to run canary traffic that asserts output quality thresholds.
[02:48] [03:00] Jordan Lee: quick note, Priya, we also elevated this under our SLA team and put a postmortem doc in the shared folder. Maya will drop the link in Slack.
[03:12] Priya Nair: thanks. On the long-term fixes \u2014 you mentioned runtime patching for GC and autoscaler behavior. What's the ETA?
[03:19] David Park: for the autoscaler policy change it's live in your env already as a config change. The GC tuning is a control-plane patch scheduled for next week \u2014 tentative rollout 2027-01-20 subject to canary passes in staging.
[03:31] Liam O'Connor: will that require downtime or redeploys on our side?
[03:34] David Park: no customer-side downtime. It's a control plane update; we'll do a canary then a gradual rollout with monitoring.
[03:43] Samira Khan: what about alerts \u2014 can we get earlier warnings before queue length spikes to avoid user impact?
[03:48] Maya Chen: yes, we're adding a new alert that looks at combined signals: queue length + KV cache miss rate + tail latency (p95/p99). We'll push recommended thresholds to your PagerDuty and to the Redwood Console.
[04:02] [04:15] Priya Nair: what about security/compliance questions? Our SecOps asked whether the incident left any logs or secrets exposed \u2014 they were worried because the incident involved control plane GC issues and scaling.
[04:25] Maya Chen: we audited the logs and there was no data plane leak. Access controls and KMS remained intact. We will share the SOC2/ISO audit excerpt and a signed attestation for the incident review.
[04:39] Priya Nair: appreciated. Please include KMS usage logs and any CPK/KMS request traces as part of evidence.
[04:47] Maya Chen: noted. We'll attach those.
[04:51] [05:00] Liam O'Connor: one ask \u2014 can you document the decision criteria for fallback and a matrix of when Redwood will choose dedicated vs fallback model? We need to present to our product folks.
[05:10] David Park: sure, we'll produce a short doc that shows routing policy inputs and example scenarios. It will include latency thresholds, token progress tests, and a quality gate.
[05:22] Priya Nair: also we want more visibility into model variants used per request for auditing. Is that available?
[05:28] Maya Chen: yes, we can enable per-request model metadata in the logs for your account; that will show model version, route chosen, and fallback reason. That will increase log volume but is useful for audits.
[05:40] [06:00] Samira Khan: about the KV cache \u2014 any plans to make eviction less brittle? It seemed a bit all-or-nothing during the spike.
[06:08] David Park: longer term we're working on adaptive cache eviction and prioritized pinning for hot prefixes. Short term we added headroom config and are monitoring miss rates. We'll propose a quantization-friendly cache tuning for your workload.
[06:23] Priya Nair: perfect. For the load test, we want to replay the exact traffic that caused the burst \u2014 batch patterns plus spikes from our analytics. Liam will share the profile.
[06:33] Liam O'Connor: yes I'll share the CSV with per-minute qps and token distribution.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: we'll schedule a joint dry-run in staging first, then a production-scale test with throttled risk windows.
[06:46] [07:00] Priya Nair: timeline for runbook updates?
[07:03] David Park: David will draft runbook edits and the mitigation checklist \u2014 including step-by-step switchback to increase cache headroom, how to force a graceful rollback of fallbacks, and how to bump autoscaler parameters. Target by 2027-01-20.
[07:18] Maya Chen: we'll also add a playbook entry for communication steps \u2014 what Sable support should do and what Redwood sends during incidents.
[07:26] [07:45] Priya Nair: can we get an SLA credit conversation? This incident exceeded our SLOs and had business impact.
[07:51] Maya Chen: yes, we'll escalate to account and legal. Jordan will own the SLA credit request; we'll include impact window and metrics.
[07:59] Jordan Lee: noted, I'll file a ticket and loop in ops/legal.
[08:05] [08:30] Liam O'Connor: quick question about private deployments \u2014 we've been exploring Redwood Private for sensitive workloads. Does this incident change anything around that?
[08:37] David Park: the root causes were runtime and control plane related, not customer isolation. Redwood Private would avoid shared control plane artifacts, but the core runtime behavior would be the same; patching and autoscaler improvements will apply across modes. We can discuss architecture differences in a separate session.
[08:55] Priya Nair: ok. We'll reconvene on Private later.
[09:00] [09:20] Maya Chen: next steps recap: 1) Maya: share incident timeline + Grafana link (by 1/17). 2) David: runbook and KB edits (by 1/20). 3) Liam/Samira: provide load profile and confirm test window (by 1/18). 4) Joint load test (week of 1/24). 5) Jordan: SLA credit ticket.
[09:35] Priya Nair: all sounds good. One more ask \u2014 please include the decision tree for model fallback in the doc. We want to show it to product.
[09:44] David Park: will do. We'll include an illustrative flowchart and a small matrix with thresholds.
[09:52] [10:00] Samira Khan: small nit: can you add an example curl of how to enable per-request model metadata? That will help our SRE quickly toggle it on for audits.
[10:08] Maya Chen: yes, we have a CLI snippet and an API param; will include both in the KB.
[10:14] Priya Nair: awesome. Anything else?
[10:18] Maya Chen: nothing from us. Thanks for the partnership and detailed notes during the incident \u2014 that made triage faster.
[10:25] Liam O'Connor: thanks, everyone.
[10:28] Priya Nair: thanks.
[10:31] [Wrap] Meeting end ~14:42 PST.
